name: Zone of Pain (Rigid Core)
description: The package contains a lot of concrete code and is stable (many dependencies), but it is difficult to change without cascading breakage (Martin's Zone of Pain).

name: Zone of Uselessness
description: The package contains many abstractions, but they are unstable and not used as a reliable foundation (Zone of Uselessness).

name: God Package (Blob)
description: An overly large, complex package with a low maintainability index. Hard to refactor and understand.

name: Coupling Hub
description: The package has critically many incoming and outgoing dependencies, creating an architectural bottleneck.

name: Unstable Utility
description: The package consists mostly of static utilities, but is unstable and changes frequently, causing ripple effects.

name: Overly Complex Implementation
description: High algorithmic complexity (Effort) and difficulty (Difficulty) of the code inside the package.

name: Error-Prone Package
description: High number of potential errors (Halstead Errors) and a large vocabulary indicate convoluted logic.

name: Interface Bloat
description: Excessive number of interfaces with few concrete implementations (possible API over-engineering).

name: Hidden Technical Debt
description: A moderate maintainability index masks high complexity and outgoing coupling. Debt accumulates covertly.

name: High Efferent Dependency
description: The package depends on too many other packages, making it brittle when changes occur in the system.

name: Kotlin Data Class Anemia
description: The package is overloaded with Kotlin data classes without complex business logic (a sign of Anemic Domain Model).

name: Kotlin Companion Object Bloat
description: Overuse of companion objects, which may indicate a return to static methods and reduced testability.
